content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat plain tortilla chips are crisp slices made from corn tortillas that are baked with less oil than traditional chips. They have a neutral flavor, making them a versatile snack and a base for a variety of dips and toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortilla chips originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a corn‑based alternative to potato chips.
The lower fat content is achieved by baking instead of deep‑frying.
They often appear in diet menus because they contain roughly 30 % fewer calories than regular chips.
Corn tortillas are naturally gluten‑free and high in fiber.
Tortilla chips are commonly served with guacamole, salsa, or yogurt‑based dips.

items.title: Reduced fat content
items.content: Less added oil makes them more suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The corn base provides a steady release of energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and can help regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Made from pure corn, they are safe for people with gluten intolerance.

items.title: Low sodium (when unsalted)
items.content: Unsalted versions help control overall sodium intake.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn and should avoid the product.

items.title: Sodium in flavored versions
items.content: Seasoned varieties can contain significant amounts of salt.

items.title: Caloric density remains
items.content: Even with reduced fat, the snack is still energy‑dense and should be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy them straight from the bag, use as a crunchy base for toppings, add to salads, soups, or make chip‑tartare. They pair well with guacamole, salsa, hummus, or yogurt dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. Once opened, consume within 2–3 weeks to retain crispness and flavor. Discard if you notice off‑flavors or signs of rancidity.
